construct: The primate lateral geniculate nucleus contains two ventral magnocellular layers and four dorsal parvocellular layers. Magnocellular inputs derive from large-field, motion-sensitive retinal ganglion cells and are specialized for rapid temporal/luminance changes and motion. Parvocellular pathways contribute more strongly to high spatial resolution and color/form processing.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A unilateral lesion restricted to LGN magnocellular layers spares parvocellular color/fine-detail processing but selectively impairs high-temporal-resolution motion/luminance processing in the contralateral visual hemifield.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Red-green color loss is a plausible visual-stream deficit, but it preferentially implicates parvocellular processing, which is explicitly spared.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The keyed response uniquely combines magnocellular function with the contralateral field localization imposed by a unilateral postchiasmal LGN lesion.
